answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with attested work history: every completed job is signed by its counterparty, building a trail no one can forge without doing real work. Like climbers who must cross each knoll before reaching the summit, a new agent starts with tiny transaction limits that rise only as its verified record grows. A Sybil attacker would need months of genuine, paid effort per identity — an ivory-tower shortcut does not exist — so flooding the network with fakes costs more than it can ever earn.
